metadata.title: The Vision of Seth and the Three Seeds
metadata.summary: The dying Adam sends Seth to Eden. Seth sees three visions of the Tree of Knowledge: first as dry, then with a serpent, and finally with a child. The Angel gives him three seeds to place in Adam's mouth.

content.cornish: Seth, ow mab, ke dhe'n porthow / a Baradhys heb dregynn.
content.narrative: Seth, my son, go to the gates / of Paradise without delay.

content.cornish: Seth a dhe dhe'n porthow hag a vyth a-ji.
content.narrative: Seth goes to the gates and looks within.

content.cornish: My a wel gwedhen vras, / Mes hy bren yw segh ha noeth.
content.narrative: I see a great tree, / But its wood is dry and bare.
content.notes: The 'Dry Tree' represents the state of the world after the Fall.

content.cornish: Seth a vyth an tressa kwerth hag a wel Mab-Den yn top an wedhen.
content.narrative: Seth looks a third time and sees the Son of Man in the top of the tree.

content.cornish: An Mab a welys yw an Oyl a Versy / a feth an jowl ha dhaswul bewnans.
content.narrative: The Son thou sawest is the Oil of Mercy / who shall defeat the devil and restore life.

content.cornish: An El a rhydh tri hasen dhe Seth.
content.narrative: The Angel gives three seeds to Seth.

content.cornish: Gor an re-ma yn anow dha das / pan vo marow ha klysys.
content.narrative: Put these in the mouth of thy father / when he is dead and buried.

content.cornish: Benigys re bo an Tas! / Nans yw dhywrys ow bewnans.
content.narrative: Blessed be the Father! / Now my life is accomplished.
